newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian floods cause crop damage worth $91 million.
newsitem.headline: Indian floods cause crop damage worth $91 million.

text.p: Heavy rains and flash floods that ravaged the southern Indian state of Andhra Pradesh last week caused 3.24 billion rupees ($91 million) worth of crop damage, officials said on Sunday.

The state's agriculture minister, S.V. Subba Reddy, said more than 1.3 million hectares (3.2 million acres) of crops were damaged in the floods, which followed seven days of cyclonic rains in the state on the Bay of Bengal coast.
More than 300 people died and 100,000 were evacuated to safety during the floods.

Paddy crops were destroyed over an area of 86,000 hectares and partly damaged over an area of 130,797 hectares. Around 329,900 hectares of groundnut crop were destroyed and 456,000 hectares were partially damaged, Reddy said.
An estimated 30,016 hectares of cotton crop were fully damaged while 25,460 hectares were partly affected. Another 35,570 hectares of other crops like chillies were damaged.
Much of the damage was done in the districts of Prakasam, Nellore, Cuddapah, Chittoor and Anantapur.
